A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V1 presents mathematical definitions, proofs, and schematic illustrations. Its statistical-learning and Monte Carlo discussions contain theoretical bounds, not original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: V2 remains theoretical throughout its main text and appendices. The new density construction and diagrams do not report experiments, simulations, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: The MPNN updates, readout, and profile operations are retained. Appendix F generalizes the architecture-equivalence argument to an operator A already allowed by v1's main formulation; it does not introduce a new proposed MPNN procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical training or evaluation. The expanded discussion of finite weighted graphs concerns theoretical approximation domains.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baselines. Newly cited GNN approaches are discussed as related work, not included in experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an executed empirical evaluation protocol. Changes to operator bounds, probability-space assumptions, and approximation constructions belong to the mathematical analysis.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or empirical case studies. The new projection construction is part of a theoretical proof.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, or empirical uncertainty estimates. The retained concentration and generalization bounds are theoretical guarantees.

E6.justification: No experimental measurements, rankings, or observed findings are added or revised. The generalization-bound expressions are equivalently reformatted; newly introduced mathematical results are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: New Section 5.4 and Appendix L develop graph-density arguments using atomless lifting, projection bofops, and convergence of induced DIDMs. V1 asserted density without this construction. V2 also generalizes Appendix F's equivalence proof beyond normalized sums, adds uniform-equicontinuity definitions, tightens several domain and boundedness assumptions, and revises the universal-approximation proof in former Appendix M.1, now N.1.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the continuity guarantee from Hölder continuity to equicontinuity, and Section 6.1 adds an explicit approximation consequence for continuous functions on graph-signals. The principal compactness, universality, and generalization claims remain; graph density was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 clarifies that the density construction concerns weighted graph shift operators with uniformly bounded weighted degree. Appendix H.1.5 explains how spherical graphops aggregate nontrivially over measure-zero neighborhoods, and N.2 clarifies the Hölder formulation's applicability. The limitations concerning implicit covering bounds and noncomputational profiles remain.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies executable implementations, computational resource details, or code/data access instructions. V2's additional constructions and explanations are mathematical rather than new computational reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V2 adds brief discussion and citations for graphon transferability, higher-order graphon networks, and Le and Jegelka's graphop-based GNN analysis, plus a Pugh reference for equicontinuity. These extend related-work coverage without substantially changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main organization are retained. Section 4.2 substantially clarifies existing profile operations, several appendix explanations and cross-references are refined, and an impact statement and author contact information are added. Later appendices are relabeled around the new Appendix L.

P2.justification: V2 substantially changes the document-wide text width, typography, and title layout. It redraws the retained graphon hierarchy as Figure 2, adds an expanded hierarchy as Figure 1, and introduces Figure 3 and additional commutative diagrams explaining existing operations and the new projection construction.

improvement.justification: V2 improves exposition, diagrams, and parts of the formal argument, and supplies a previously absent density construction. However, new Theorem L.5 asserts convergence for equipartitions without conditions ensuring they resolve the signal; equal cell measures alone are insufficient. This leaves a gap in the principal new proof, while new Corollary I.10 stops before stating its conclusion. These defects alongside the useful additions prevent a confident judgment of net quality improvement.
